options.content: **Which rules are earning their place.** A rule that never fires is protecting nobody; a rule that fires on everything is noise an analyst learns to ignore. Shadow rules appear separately — they are evaluated against live traffic and record what they would have caught, without raising alerts.

panels.title: Alerts contributed, by rule
panels.description: Counts every rule that contributed to an alert, not just the strongest — three weak hits and one strong hit reach a similar score but mean different things.

panels.title: Shadow hits, by rule
panels.description: What rules under evaluation would have flagged. Nothing here has raised an alert — this is the evidence used to decide whether to promote a rule to ENABLED.

panels.title: Rule fire rate over time
panels.description: A rule whose rate suddenly changes without a corresponding change in traffic is usually a tuning problem, not a fraud wave.

panels.title: Risk score distribution
panels.description: Where scores actually land. A distribution piled against the alert threshold means the weights are doing very little work.

panels.title: Rule evaluation failures
panels.description: A rule that throws is contained and counted rather than taking the pipeline down. Anything above zero here needs looking at.
